liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Candyman** (2 reviews): Reviewer says Jerry sings unusually sweetly here, and calls it the first Candyman; Reviewer notes different lyrics in the first Candyman and Friend of the Devil in the acoustic set [12][16]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (2 reviews): Reviewer likes the Not Fade Away into Lovelight pairing, wishing it had been done more often later; Reviewer points to the intensity at the end of Lovelight, with Pigpen screaming the last 'ow' [14][23]
- **Dancing in the Streets** (1 review): Reviewer praises the interplay on Dancing in the Streets, with Phil and Jerry locked in throughout [17]
- **Deep Elem Blues** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Garcia's sweet vocal on Deep Elem Blues, along with Black Peter [12]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): Reviewer says Black Peter captures what makes this show special [23]
- **Katie Mae** (1 review): Reviewer finds this Katie Mae better than others, with Pigpen more at ease than in the February shows [16]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Reviewer hears Weir paying homage to Pigpen, not imitating him, when Good Lovin' and Lovelight were revived [13]

## Setlist highlights

- **Wake Up Little Susie**: rare: 9 archived performances [24]
- **Pigpen Intro - Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **Katie Mae**: rare: 10 archived performances [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1970-04-03.119118.sbd.dan.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 130 min; rated 5/5 by 3 [1]. Said about its sound: Source had monitor noise like an unshielded cable, plus oversaturation from analog recorder clipping, which were reduced [1]
- **gd70-04-03.sbd.cotsman.4283.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 124 min; rated 4.38/5 by 8 [4]. Said about its sound: Sound is pretty good; Casey Jones fades in and an occasional buzzing noise is present; Reviewer finds sound quality good, and thinks most listeners would rate it highly; Sound is okay, but quite good for the period [12][14][17][18]
- **gd1970-04-03.sbd.boswell.smith.114569.flac24**: soundboard; 22 songs; 130 min; rated 3.33/5 by 3 [2]
- **gd1970-04-03.sbd.boswell.smith.114616.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 130 min [3]

## Around the show

- The band played in a rickety old field house [15]
- The show includes an acoustic set [17]
- Reviewer attended as a toddler; their father was involved in the local music scene, including Ludlow Garage, and met the entourage [18]
- The show includes an acoustic set [23]
- Pigpen sounds more relaxed than at the February shows, per the reviewer [16]
- Reviewer considers this source a slight upgrade over another source [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1970-04-03.119118.sbd.dan.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Dan McDonald; source: MR>R>FLAC [1]. Also: Uploader cleaned the source with Diamond Cut/Forensics 8.1 [1]
- **gd70-04-03.sbd.cotsman.4283.sbefail.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]. Also: This copy is properly pitched, tested against other recordings, with China Cat in G rather than F [20]
- **gd1970-04-03.sbd.boswell.smith.114569.flac24**: taped by Will Boswell; transferred by Matt Smith; source: SBD MR>R>FLAC; Monitor Noise throughout show; tranfer Matt Smith 7/2011 [2]
- **gd1970-04-03.sbd.boswell.smith.114616.flac16**: transferred by Matt Smith; source: SBD MR>R>FLAC; Converted to 16 bit via r8brain high > TLH level 6 flac; tranfer Matt Smith 7/2011 [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Field House, U. of Cincinnati, Poster](https://www.dead.net/archives/1970/artwork/field-house-u-cincinnati-poster) [25]
